title: I've built hundreds of trading bots over the past year and this week I'm running the 12 best at once for the first time to see which is best
author: DadsGamesandCharles

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
same start day for all twelve is what makes it a fair race. one week is mostly noise though, the order will reshuffle a few times before it means anything. I made Quantradin for this kind of bake-off: every bot replays years of US stock history first, then they trade side by side on paper, free. quantradin.com

same tickers for all twelve, or does each pick its own?

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body: Some are the same tickers, some aren't. Most of these bots are made from one main version and those are the ones that usually trade the same tickers but their strategies for handling them is different.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: then the same-ticker group is worth reading apart from the rest. if four bots share a base version and tickers, a good week for one is likely a good week for all four, so the leaderboard could look like four winners when it's one idea counted four times.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body: No, each account/strategy is different, I do see what you mean but even though they share a parent, they’re not the parent or their siblings. So to speak.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair enough, then the board is twelve real entrants. the one leak left is the market itself: all twelve sit in the same week, so a trend week flatters every long bot at once. a second week with a different tape sorts that out better than any tweak.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
that's kinda why I mentioned it'll run longer than a week

also, it would only flatter the bots that are built for that specific week really, and you can tell which ones those are when it happens, plus you'll know (or you should) already which bots/algos are going to perform on which days after about 10am est because they're either already done or well into their strategy for the day.

Some of them buy once, some buy the same stock more than once, some buy multiple stocks, some buy those same stocks again throughout the day on dips, some sit out (Grok loves to do that), and some buy at open and just sell at specific times.

I already know which of these is going to win the overall contest, no matter how long it runs. If I base it off consistency, reliability, and safety then Charles 2.0 wins hands down, no questions, it's how he's built. If I base it off profit reliability, then Strategy 9 will win, it's a dip chain strategy that consistenly outperforms everything else monetarily but it's scary to watch. I've just seen these things perform for so long, that;'s where my money is.
